# v0.1.7: Cloudflare Computer study (sub-issue of #155)

Sub-issue of [#155](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/155).

One of three external studies feeding the v0.1.7 architecture refactor
migration, alongside the Drive9 study and the AgentFS study. They complement
the internal exploration study
([#156](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/156)): #156 maps what
LayerFS is; these three map the design space around it.

Cloudflare Computer ([cloudflare/computer](https://github.com/cloudflare/computer),
preview) is a **virtual filesystem that lives inside a Durable Object**: the DO
holds the authoritative state in SQLite and exposes one pluggable execution
surface through `workspace.runtime`. Three backends ship today — **container**
(sandbox-side `computerd` mounts the state as a real FUSE filesystem and syncs
changes back over a capnweb RPC channel), **isolate shell** (just-bash in a
Dynamic Worker reaching the workspace over Workers RPC), and **isolate
JavaScript** (an ECMAScript module in a Dynamic Worker with Workspace-backed
`node:fs/promises` plus trusted `ws:git` and `ws:artifacts` modules). Backends
register under stable IDs behind a single
`workspace.runtime.exec(source, { backend })` entry point and connect lazily; a
Workspace can also exist with no backend at all — the filesystem on its own.

The interesting shape for LayerFS: a strict authority/projection split — one
authoritative store, execution surfaces as projections of it — that echoes, and
stresses, the Store/Workspace relationship the v0.1.7 refactor is reworking.

## Goal

A source-backed breakdown of Cloudflare Computer:

- **Architecture:** the Durable Object as sole authority; how state, sync and
  execution are separated; what `computerd`, `dofs` and the RPC layer each own;
  the numbered spec series `docs/01_vfs.md` … `docs/19_performance.md` as the
  map.
- **Implementation details:** the sandbox-to-DO sync protocol
  (`docs/02_sync_protocol.md`), the SQLite filesystem schema
  (`docs/03_filesystem_schema.md`), the mount interface (`docs/06`), lifecycle
  (`docs/11`), the backend registry and lazy-connection model, and the
  container/isolate split (`docs/12`, `16`, `17`).
- **Interface:** `workspace.runtime.exec` as the single execution entry point;
  the `fs` and `runtime` surfaces of `@cloudflare/computer`; the tool, git,
  assets and artifacts interfaces (`docs/09`, `13`, `14`, `15`).
- **What LayerFS can learn — the point of the study:** authority placement and
  projection, the pluggable-execution-backends pattern (one entry point, stable
  IDs, lazy connect), the sync-protocol design, single-DO concurrency
  constraints versus LayerFS's Store, and which parts of their spec series are
  worth borrowing for LayerFS's own documentation — and which parts do not fit.

## Deliverable

One document under `docs/roadmap/0.1/0.1.7/study/cloudflare-computer/` (folder
initialized with this work item), linked from the
[v0.1.7 checklist](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/main/docs/roadmap/0.1/0.1.7/README.md)
when accepted. It records the exact snapshot commit it was written against.

## Sources

- Upstream: https://github.com/cloudflare/computer (preview only; APIs
  unstable, and the spec under `docs/` is forward-looking — read it for intent,
  not as description of the code today)
- Local snapshot: `/Users/yifanxu/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/study/cloudflare-computer`
  @ `64c462b` (2026-08-26, "bench: account for spawned computerd tasks")
- In-tree docs: the numbered spec series `docs/01_vfs.md` …
  `docs/19_performance.md`; runnable consumers under `examples/`

## Boundary

- Source reads against the pinned local snapshot only: no builds, tests or
  benchmarks of the studied repo, no changes to it, and no LayerFS code changes
  from this issue.
- The preview caveat applies: claims are checked against the code, not taken
  from the spec alone; spec statements are labelled as intent.
- Every load-bearing claim carries a source reference (file, module or doc);
  behaviour that could not be verified is recorded as unknown.
- Performance claims are quoted only from Cloudflare's own material with
  citations; this study measures nothing.
- Observations that imply a LayerFS change are handed to the v0.1.7 checklist,
  not decided here.

## Starting map (snapshot, orientation only)

A descriptive snapshot to start from, not a frozen scope and not a substitute
for the study's own source reads.

```text
packages/
  computer/                       # DO filesystem + runtime surface (src/{client,backends,mounts,git,artifacts,assets,observe})
  computerd/                      # sandbox-side daemon: FUSE mount + sync over capnweb
  dofs/ rpc/                      # Durable Object filesystem + capnweb RPC layer
  computer-computerd-linux-x64/   # prebuilt computerd binary
docs/                             # numbered spec: 01_vfs … 19_performance
examples/                         # container, worker-shell, worker-javascript
```

## Status

Open. Created at owner direction, 2026-09-16; initialized only. The detailed
study structure is written with the study.

comments.body:
**Study complete — deliverable written 2026-09-16.**

**Deliverable:** `docs/roadmap/0.1/0.1.7/study/cloudflare-computer/architecture_overview.md` (786 lines: prose + citations + four architecture figures — deployment topology, the exec round trip, the sync consistency model, and the backend routing shape — plus the concept-mapping table, observations with verdicts, unknowns, and source index).
**SHA-256:** `84f6e0aaaeebd7425b9694a8c3f27f9eda99e90dfdea2956f32aa7df4132a554`
**Pin:** upstream `https://github.com/cloudflare/computer` (preview; APIs unstable, spec forward-looking); pinned local snapshot `/Users/yifanxu/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/study/cloudflare-computer` at `64c462b083860cad29b374b9e4cda1e6a680f902` (2026-08-26, "bench: account for spawned computerd tasks").

**Research log:**

- Eight areas, one research subagent each, run in parallel: (1) Durable Object authority & schema, (2) sync protocol, mounts & capnweb wire, (3) runtime & backend registry, (4) container backend & FUSE, (5) isolate backends, (6) fs/tools/observe surfaces, (7) git/assets/artifacts interfaces, (8) lifecycle, performance claims & the doc-by-doc spec-vs-code audit. One split change vs. the issue's suggested seven: "auxiliary interfaces" was split in two (fs/tools/observe vs. git/assets/artifacts — the latter is ~1,600 lines of spec plus three packages).
- Verification: ~30 citation spot-checks across all eight reports (3–5 per report), all confirmed, plus first-hand reads of the load-bearing sources — the capnweb wire contract (`packages/rpc/src/interface.ts`), the backend contract (`backend.ts`), the dofs schema (`schema/core.ts`, `schema/sync.ts`), the runtime router, and `docs/02_sync_protocol.md` / `docs/19_performance.md` in full.
- Reconciliation: one subagent claim discarded after direct contradiction (computerd ships TypeScript sources, not a dist-only package); one cross-report disagreement settled by code check (exec-log retention — 5 min / 16 MiB — is implemented, not doc-only).
- Read-only everywhere: exactly one file written (the deliverable), nothing under `study/` modified, no builds/tests/benchmarks of either repo, nothing measured.

**Strongest "what LayerFS can learn" findings** (full detail, concept table, and verdicts in the deliverable):

1. **Adopt the rebuild-everything recovery discipline.** The DO SQLite is the only durable state; every projection (container VFS, capnweb sessions, exec logs) is reconstructible from cursors and rev-0 rebaselines. Nothing durable may live in a projection — this constrains v0.1.7's seam placement.
2. **Adopt the narrow backend contract as internal v0.1.7 structure.** `backend.ts` is 105 lines: backends register an id and produce handles that declare `sync: "remote"|"none"` and transport liveness; two backend protocols, one runtime path. Not yet a public extension point.
3. **Borrow-with-changes the exec bracket.** A failed pre-exec push aborts before spawn; a failed post-exec pull becomes a durable retry (DO alarms) fenced to the container's runtime UUID, terminating in `EEXEC_LOST`/`lost` rather than silently succeeding against an empty VFS. Directly transferable to 0.2 pending-Proposal reconnect/crash recovery.
4. **Borrow the haves/wants negotiation shape, not the store.** State-based sync (final-state entries + tombstones, `(rev, path)` resume cursor, bytes only by hash after a probe) validates the batch-shaped `ObjectStore` seam in cloud-sqlite-vfs §2(c); avoid the history-less store and the fixed 512 KiB chunking (their own doc defers CDC and names the head-insertion cost).
5. **Not-applicable as semantics, adopt as practice: the conflict honesty.** Their docs state plainly which concurrent patterns lose data (last-writer-wins, no detection, no merge) and refuse to pretend the workspace is a CRDT — confirming 0.2's reconciliation task is real work, not gold-plating.
6. **Adopt wire-checkable invariants.** Every push/fetch echoes the receiver's `appliedPushCursor` and the sender asserts coverage; "receiver is caught up" is inspectable on the wire instead of load-bearing in-process state.
7. **Borrow for any hosted-store design (D1-A).** The system contains no locking code; the platform serializes, and on top there is exactly one application-level serializer (a per-backend mutation FIFO, reads bypass). The one-writer invariant as an auditable server property, via cursors plus echoed assertions.
8. **Borrow-with-changes, selectively: container daemon engineering.** Replay-safety policy ("may have started, was not replayed" — never double-execute on ambiguous dispatch); runtime-identity UUID separating reconnect from replacement; durable (not per-connect) secrets; fail-closed "peer must enforce auth" checks; exec env allowlists; `cd`-quoting around the uv_spawn/FUSE deadlock; mount-before-listen.
9. **Borrow-with-changes for 0.2: execution observability.** Every exec has an id and monotonic seq, streams live, replays from a log, and settles a typed result carrying its own sync accounting (`pushed/pulled/skipped`) — the shape of resumable work at the execution layer.
10. **Borrow-with-changes: numbered docs only with living status banners.** At this pin the spec series drifts in both directions (the README denies a mount subsystem that ships; docs promise lazy mounts that don't exist; two docs cite commits absent from the local history). A spec series without maintained status labels inverts from description to folklore.

**Unknowns** (recorded in the deliverable): platform semantics behind vendor claims (DO input-gate serialization, `transactionSync` atomicity, Worker Loader isolate caching and `cpuMs` enforcement, OOM isolation, whether the ~10 GB cap is enforced anywhere); snapshot provenance (the local git history is authored by the snapshot owner rather than upstream; docs cite commits `dc692c0`/`c952c4d` that don't resolve locally; the deployed-bench script pins a different upstream commit `de87919a`); capnweb wire framing and binary-frame behavior (library-internal); `file://` git transport advertised but likely broken (no transport registered); whether the unused-in-repo `exec-wire.ts` has external consumers; whether GHCR tag `0.2.1` matches this source tree; the tree-shaking claim verified by packaging construction, not measurement; exact error text for dropped optional shell commands; the keep-alive alarm referenced in `health-probe.ts:7` has no in-tree call site.

These observations are handed to the #155 checklist as recommendations, not decisions.

#158 remains open for acceptance.

title: v0.1.7: Cloudflare Computer study — Durable Object virtual filesystem: architecture, implementation, interface, and what LayerFS can learn
